userStories.title: Add host-side audit log writer (JSONL on disk)
userStories.description: As the host studio, I want every accepted RPC, kick, rotate, and kill-switch event appended to a per-session JSONL audit log on host disk so the persistent record stays local (matching the trust model: payload bytes never leave the host machine).
acceptanceCriteria: Working dir: /Users/tuongaz/dev/seeflow

Per design doc lines 263 + 176: audit log lives at `~/.seeflow/share-history/<sessionId>.jsonl`. Justification: the trust model puts source-of-truth on host disk; durable audit on DDB/S3 would leak peer activity off-host, violating the 'relay never persists payload' invariant

Create `apps/studio/src/share-audit.ts` exporting `AuditEntry` type and `createAuditLogger(sessionId: string, root?: string)` returning `{ append(entry: Omit<AuditEntry, 'ts'>): Promise<void>; list(opts?: { limit?: number; cursor?: number }): Promise<{ entries: AuditEntry[]; nextCursor: number | null }>; close(): Promise<void> }`

`AuditEntry` shape: `{ ts: number; peerId: string | null; displayName: string | null; kind: 'rpc-accept' | 'rpc-reject' | 'kick' | 'rotate' | 'kill-switch' | 'host-start' | 'host-stop' | 'peer-join' | 'peer-leave'; op?: string; reason?: string; details?: Record<string, unknown> }`
`append` writes one JSON line, newline-terminated, via `atomic-write`-style append (fs.appendFile with exclusive flag handling for concurrent writes)

`list` reads the JSONL file with line-by-line streaming, returns up to `limit` (default 200) entries starting at byte offset `cursor` (default 0), and `nextCursor` is the byte offset to resume (null on EOF). Reverse-chronological NOT required — UI sorts
Directory `~/.seeflow/share-history/` is created via `fs.mkdir({recursive:true})` on first append; root override exists for tests

Create `apps/studio/src/share-audit.test.ts` with a tempdir root covering: append 1000 entries → list paginates correctly; concurrent appends from 10 parallel promises preserve all entries (no interleaving corruption); list on missing file returns `{entries:[], nextCursor:null}`
